statement: A restarted node never records recovery_ready_held while distributed transaction replay is incomplete or failed. The startup runtime handoff publishes a typed transaction_recovery_incomplete outcome with the exact failed decision dimension and route source whenever replay stops short of completion, and that evidence outranks generic admission load in failure classification. Poison durable transaction-row state is attributed to its owning writer/replay path rather than patched inside bootstrap.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Transaction replay is owned by the startup runtime handoff boundary, not the bootstrap routing phase. A replay that stops short of completion must surface as a typed transaction_recovery_incomplete outcome carrying the exact failed decision dimension and route source; bootstrap must never mint a recovery-ready witness over incomplete replay.

Repeated poison durable transaction-row state is attributed to its owning writer/replay path. Compare alternate-route and forced-canonical-seed restarts: if both routes reach the same exact TRANSACTION_RECOVERY_INCOMPLETE predicate after canonical authority is consumed, route ownership is discharged and the writer/replay invariant owns the fix; if the fatal follows only the alternate route, the routing handoff owns that repair.
Do not patch transaction-recovery correctness inside bootstrap seed-contact or routing code. The invariant belongs to the distributed transaction writer/replay owner.

Closure requires the repository-mandated controlled live A/B (fixed node count, workload, failure schedule, clean-start protocol, source fingerprint) proving a poisoned transaction row produces the typed outcome and correct owner attribution, never nodeAdmissionBlocked masking the causal fatal.
